headline: Approved ferry terminal variance at 10 Blaney Street and garage and sunroom at 23 Jackson Street; several other petitions continued.
summary: Approved a variance for a new two-story ferry terminal building at 10 Blaney Street. Approved a variance and special permit for a sunroom, attached garage, and entry deck at 23 Jackson Street. Continued four petitions and allowed one withdrawal, at 61 Memorial Drive.
decisions: Allowed withdrawal without prejudice, 5-0, of the variance petition of Amy Pelletier for a shed at 61 Memorial Drive.
Approved 5-0 a variance to build a two-story ferry terminal building on the property line of 10 Blaney Street and 71 Derby Street, with standard and special conditions.

Continued 5-0, to August 19, 2026, the petition of Graham Wing (formerly Graham Hines) for a variance to divide a merged parcel at 7 Burnside Street and 5 Skerry Street Court and build a two-family house.
Approved 5-0 a variance and special permit to build a sunroom, attached two-car garage, and modified entry deck at 23 Jackson Street, raising lot coverage from 25.4% to 36% where 35% is required.
Continued 5-0, to August 19, 2026, the petition of Israel Berl for variances to create a 45-foot curb cut and five-car parking area at 2 Rockdale Avenue.
Continued 5-0, to a special meeting on July 29, 2026, the special permit petition of Carrie Ditcher at 21 Warren Street.
Continued 5-0, to a special meeting on July 29, 2026, the special permit petition of Robert Beverly at 46 Chestnut Street.
Approved the June 17, 2026 meeting minutes as drafted, with all members in favor.

City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals 
Meeting Minutes 
July 15, 2026 
 
A meeting of the Salem Zoning Board of Appeals (“Salem ZBA”) was held on Wednesday, July 15, 
2026 at 6:30 pm via remote participation in accordance with Section 30A of Chapter 20 of the Acts of 2021, as 
amended by Section 40 of Chapter 2 of the Acts of 2023, and further amended by Section 1 of Chapter 2 of the 
Acts of 2025, the City is authorized to conduct remote meetings of its public bodies through June 30, 2027.  
 
Chair Vyedin calls the meeting to order at 6:30 pm. 
Chair Vyedin explains how individuals can participate in the meeting remotely via Zoom, and that 
instructions to participate remotely can also be found on the Salem website.  Ms. Vyedin also 
explains the rules regarding public comment. 
 
ROLL CALL  
Those present were: Chair Nina Vyedin, Vice Chair Christa McGaha, Ellen Simpson, Peter Habib, 
Elena Eimert, and Stephen Larrick.  Also in attendance were Brennan Postich — Staff Planner, and 
Voula Orfanos — Building Commissioner.  Those absent were: None 
 
CONTINUANCES   
Location: 61 Memorial Drive (Map 42, Lot 0014) (R1 Zoning District) 
Applicant: Amy Pelletier 
Project: A public hearing for all persons interested in the petition of AMY PELLETIER at 61 
MEMORIAL DRIVE (Map 42, Lot 0014) (R1 Zoning District; Coastal Resiliency 
Overlay District) for a Variance per Section 3.2.4 Accessory Structures of the Salem 
Zoning Ordinance to construct a two-story, eight-foot by sixteen-foot shed with a 
gross floor area of approximately 256 square feet. 
 
 
Documents and Exhibitions     
• Application date-stamped May 20, 2026, and supporting documentation 
 
Vice Chair McGaha introduces the petition and notes that the applicant has requested to withdraw 
without prejudice. 
 
Vice Chair McGaha opens the floor to public comment, but there is none. 
 
Motion and Vote: Ms. Simpson motions to withdraw without prejudice the petition of AMY 
PELLETIER at 61 MEMORIAL DRIVE (Map 42, Lot 0014) (R1 Zoning District; Coastal 
Resiliency Overlay District) for a Variance per Section 3.2.4 Accessory Structures of the Salem 
Zoning Ordinance to construct a two-story, eight-foot by sixteen-foot shed with a gross floor area 
of approximately 256 square feet.
City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals 
July 15, 2026 Meeting Minutes

Mr. Habib seconds the motion.  The vote is five (5) in favor (Christa McGaha, Nina Vyedin, 
Ellen Simpson, Peter Habib, and Elena Eimert) and none (0) opposed.  The motion passes. 
 
REGULAR AGENDA   
Location: 10 Blaney Street (Map 41, Lot 0278) (I Zoning District; Coastal Resiliency Overlay 
District) 
Applicant: The Salem Harbor Port Authority 
Project: A public hearing for all persons interested in the petition of the SALEM HARBOR 
PORT AUTHORITY at 10 BLANEY STREET (Map 41, Lot 0278; Map 41, Lot 
0342) (I Zoning District; Coastal Resiliency Overlay District) for a Variance per 
Section 4.1.1 Dimensional Requirements of the Salem Zoning Ordinance to construct 
a two-story ferry terminal building on the property line of 10 Blaney Street and 71 
Derby Street, where a thirty-foot setback is required. The building would be located 
near an existing ferry terminal. Additionally, the Applicant requests a six-month 
extension to exercise rights granted by the Variance decision. 
 
 
Documents and Exhibitions     
• Application date-stamped June 22, 2026, and supporting documentation 
 
Chair Vyedin introduces the petition. 
 
Bill McHugh introduces himself as the director of the Salem Harbor Port Authority and introduces 
his team.  Mr. McHugh explains that the proposal is to replace what was supposed to be a temporary 
structure.  The plumbing and HVAC systems of the existing terminal building are failing, according 
to Mr. McHugh, and the structure needs replacing due to growth as well.  Mr. McHugh indicates the 
shape of the lot is odd and difficult to accommodate large structures, and that the plans have been 
scaled down, but that the proposal is based on functionality needs.  Proximity to ferry landings, 
proximity to point access area, accessibility, and lot configurations and dimensions are discussed.  
Mr. McHugh discusses the setbacks and presents a certified plot plan and dimensional table showing 
existing conditions.   
 
Deborah Fennick of Fennick McCredie Architects introduces herself as project architect and 
provides additional details of the proposed new Salem Ferry terminal, which she states would serve 
as a permanent, resilient, and modern gateway hub for waterborne transportation.  The terminal will 
provide passenger services and operations such as ticketing, waiting areas, restrooms, and 
concession support, with operational capacity for current and future tourism needs.  There is 
leasable space on the second level of the building, hopefully for a maritime-related entity.  Ms. 
Fennick also discusses port operations and resiliency and sustainability-related design elements, such 
as an elevated first floor, durable materials, and provision for a future solar array.  Ms. Fennick 
explains the proposed massing and building design, highlighting efficiency and compactness. 
 
Aaron Udy of Fennick McCredie Architects introduces himself and presents a plot plan showing the 
proposed building, and identifies the velocity zone, low water mark, and building egress.  He 
presents additional, more detailed plans and discusses vehicle and pedestrian access.  The plans 
show both the existing and proposed building, emergency vehicle access, and the designated velocity
City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals 
July 15, 2026 Meeting Minutes 
  3 
zone.  Mr. Udy notes blue bike and regular bike racks, as well as the harbor walk and wastewater 
facilities. 
 
Daniel Collins of the Salem Harbor Port Authority introduces himself and discusses the constraints 
of the building area, zoning setbacks, and property conditions.  Mr. Collins presents a map 
highlighting the long, narrow shape of the lot and existing nonconformities.  Mr. Collins also 
discusses compliance with the Coastal Resiliency Overlay District requirements and how it impacted 
design elements of the proposal, including setbacks and proximity to the property at 71 Derby 
Street.  Mr. Collins explains the variance request and the hardships related to the uniqueness of the 
site.  He also speaks to the public benefits of the proposed project. 
 
Mr. Udy discusses the proposed site circulation further and also presents a diagram showing the 
proposed building height and flood elevations.  A rendering of the proposed structure is also shown, 
and Mr. Udy notes accessibility as well as design elements.  Mr. Udy presents exterior elevations and 
concludes. 
 
Chair Vyedin acknowledges the uniqueness of the lot as a hardship, and asks for further clarification 
regarding the setbacks shown on the plot plans.  Chair Vyedin suggests the vote should be on a zero 
setback rather than a 2.3-foot setback after clarification.  She also asks about easements relative to 
the potential for the building to encroach upon the abutting plot, despite it also being city-owned.  
Ms. Simpson asks for clarification regarding the velocity zone.  Mr. Collins explains the velocity 
zone further as the area where the worst waves would hit during a flood, and best practices of not 
building within the velocity zone.  Mr. Udy also provides additional comment regarding the velocity 
zone and potential flooding.  The Board discusses the lot lines and abutting properties further.  Ms. 
McGaha suggests a letter in support of the neighboring property after clarification that one is city 
property and one is port authority property.  Mr. Larrick agrees it would be good as a special 
condition. 
 
Chair Vyedin opens the floor to public comment. 
 
John Tierney of 3 White Street introduces himself as an abutter to the parking lot.  Mr. Tierney asks 
if the variance would allow for building at any height, noting concerns about abutters’ views being 
obstructed.  He questions the need for offices on the second floor, a function room, and suggests a 
one-level building not larger than the existing building should suffice.     
 
Chair Vyedin and Mr. Collins confirm that there is not a variance being requested for height.  Mr. 
McHugh speaks to the space requirements and needs.  Ms. Eimert further clarifies height 
requirements related to the CROD. 
 
Chair Vyedin notes the requested special condition for a six-month extension to exercise rights 
granted by the variance decision to allow for adequate time for construction.  She also notes the 
previously discussed special condition regarding the side setback and dimensional table, as well as 
the special condition for a letter from the port authority, which owns the neighboring parcel, to 
confirm the development is allowed to encroach on the property line. 
 
The petitioners discuss timing, funding, Chapter 91, and construction requirements related to the 
request for an extension to exercise the variance rights, noting an optimistic timeline for a completed 
project is three years.
City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals 
July 15, 2026 Meeting Minutes 
  4 
 
Motion and Vote: Ms. Eimert motions to approve the petition of SALEM HARBOR PORT 
AUTHORITY at 10 BLANEY STREET (Map 41, Lot 0278; Map 41, Lot 0342) (I Zoning District; 
Coastal Resiliency Overlay District) for a Variance per Section 4.1.1 Dimensional Requirements of 
the Salem Zoning Ordinance to construct a two-story ferry terminal building on the property line of 
10 Blaney Street and 71 Derby Street, where a thirty-foot setback is required. The building would be 
located near an existing ferry terminal.  The approval is subject to the following standard 
conditions:. 
1. Petitioner shall comply with all city and state statutes, ordinances, codes, and regulations. 
2. All construction shall be done as per the plans and dimensions submitted to and 
approved by the Building Commissioner. 
3. All requirements of the Salem Fire Department relative to smoke and fire safety shall be 
strictly adhered to. 
4. Petitioner shall obtain a building permit prior to beginning any construction. 
5. A Certificate of Occupancy is t be obtained. 
6. A Certificate of Inspection is to be obtained. 
7. Petitioner is to obtain approval from any City Board or Commission having jurisdiction 
including, but not limited to, the Planning Board. 
8. Unless this Decision expressly provides otherwise, any zoning relief granted does not 
empower or authorize the Petitioner to demolish or reconstruct the structure(s) located 
on the subject property to an extent of more than fifty percent (50%) of its floor area or 
more than fifty percent (50%) of its replacement cost at the time of destruction.  If the 
structure is demolished by any means to an extent of more than fifty percent (50%) of its 
replacement cost or more than fifty percent (50%) of its floor area at the time of 
destruction, it shall not be reconstructed except in conformity with the provisions of the 
Ordinance. 
9. All construction shall be done per the plans and dimensions submitted to and approve 
by this Board.  Any modification to the plans and dimensions must be approved by the 
Board of Appeals unless such changes are deemed a minor field change by the Building 
Commissioner in consultation with the Chair of the Board of Appeals. 
10. Petitioner shall schedule Assessing Department inspections of the property, at least 
annually, to project completion and a final inspection upon project completion. 
 
And the following special conditions: 
   1.  The petitioner shall submit a revised dimensional table for the plot plan dated July 7,  
        2026, by Nitsch Engineering, showing a revised zero-foot side setback, to the  
        Inspectional Services department prior to receiving a building permit. 
   2.  The petitioner shall submit a letter of permission from the property owner verifying   
        that the construction of the ferry terminal building can be located on 67/71 Derby   
        Street, to the Planning Department prior to receiving a building permit. 
   3.  Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the Board will consider rights authorized by  
       the Variance exercised so long as the City timely records the Board’s decision and  
       diligently pursues all necessary Planning Board approvals and a Chapter 91 license. 
 
Mr. Habib seconds the motion.  The vote is five (5) in favor (Ellen Simpson, Peter Habib, 
Elena Eimert, Nina Vyedin, and Christa McGaha) and none (0) opposed.  The motion 
passes.
City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals 
July 15, 2026 Meeting Minutes 
  5 
   
Location: 7 Burnside Street and 5 Skerry Street Court (Map 36, Lot 0157; Map 36, Lot 0149) 
(R2 Zoning District) 
Applicant: Graham Wing (formerly Graham Hines) 
Project: A public hearing for all persons interested in the petition of GRAHAM WING 
(formerly Graham Hines) at 7 BURNSIDE STREET and 5 SKERRY STREET 
COURT (Map 36, Lot 0157; Map 36, Lot 0149) (R2 Zoning District) for a Variance 
per Section 4.1.1 Dimensional Requirements of the Salem Zoning Ordinance to divide 
an existing merged parcel and construct a two-family house at 5 Skerry Street Court. 
The proposal would create a 4,393-square-foot lot at 7 Burnside Street with a 2,196-
square-foot lot area per dwelling unit, and a 3,820-square-foot lot at 5 Skerry Street 
Court with a 1,910-square-foot lot area per dwelling unit, thirty-seven-foot frontage, 
and insufficient front, side, and rear setbacks. 
 
 
Documents and Exhibitions     
• Application date-stamped May 28, 2026, and supporting documentation 
 
Chair Vyedin introduces the petition. 
 
Attorney Bill Quinn introduces himself on behalf of the petitioner and explains that this is a unique 
petition that would allow two plots that have merged to be legally separated and modified to create 
two lots.  Mr. Quinn explains that the front lot has an existing two-family dwelling and there will be 
no changes to the dwelling under the proposal.  The rear lot is proposed to be a building site for 
three-bedroom townhouse condominiums.  Mr. Quinn presents plot plans showing existing and 
proposed conditions and discusses lot frontage and setbacks.  He discusses the relief being requested 
and proposed 12-foot easement that will exist at the front on Burnside Street to the property line of 
the rear parcel.  Mr. Quinn notes the three parking spaces for the townhomes on the site plan.  Mr. 
Quinn acknowledges comments and concerns raised by neighbors, but suggests many concerns can 
be assuaged by special conditions to the proposed variance.  He suggests a condition prohibiting 
short-term rentals, and speaks to concerns about the number of inhabitants and subdivisions.  He 
also notes concerns regarding drainage, and contends more work will be done to ensure that there 
are no surface water or drainage issues.  Mr. Quinn also notes that no trees are planned to be 
removed and that any trimming would be consistent with any city tree ordinances.  Mr. Quinn 
indicates many of the well-written objections appear to be written by individuals that are quite 
knowledgeable about zoning law, but also notes that zoning law on variances in towns and cities in 
Massachusetts all changed on July 1, 2026, as part of the state budget act.  Mr. Quinn contends the 
changes are intended to make it easier to build housing and to modify the hardship criteria 
requirements.  Chair Vyedin provides clarifications regarding the updated criteria. 
 
Chair Vyedin asks clarifying questions regarding the lot lines and the subdivision.  Mr. Quinn 
discusses the division on the plot plan.  Mr. Quinn also presents an overhead street view of the area 
and plot.  Elevations of the proposal are presented, and Timeus Mulinge introduces himself as one 
of the project designers and architects.  Mr. Mulinge presents floor plans for the proposed 
townhouses and discusses design concepts, made for single-family living.  He also discusses 
elevation details and building height, which is below the limit.  Renderings of the proposed 
townhomes are shown.  Mr. Quinn discusses the requested relief and presents a dimensional table
City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals 
July 15, 2026 Meeting Minutes 
  6 
for both lots resulting from the subdivision and proposed construction.  The Board discusses the 
frontage and where it should be calculated for each lot.  Mr. Habib asks about the timing of 
purchase and merging of the two lots, and the petitioner clarifies that the second parcel that merged 
was purchased after 7 Burnside Street.  Mr. Habib suggests that the timing of the purchase might 
make the hardship self-imposed.  Ms. Simpson indicates she is usually in favor of additional housing 
but has some concerns about this project, particularly with respect to drainage, snow removal, and 
density.  She notes that the renderings of the two townhouses did not show them in the context of 
the surrounding area and dwellings, but that it would be helpful, especially with the Skerry Street 
homes.  Mr. Habib expresses concerns regarding setbacks and echoes Ms. Simpson’s concerns.  Mr. 
Eimert asks why frontage cannot be taken from Skerry Street Court and accessing the property from 
there is not viable.  Mr. Wing indicates that in previous proposals to build on this lot, there were 
issues concerning parking and traffic on Skerry Street Court.  Mr. Wing contends that having access 
and trash for both lots be on Burnside Street was meant to prevent any issues and address prior 
concerns raised.  Ms. McGaha agrees with concerns raised by other Board members, and also asks 
that the question of frontage and the legal definition be further addressed if the petition is 
continued.  Mr. Larrick asks about the initial intent when purchasing the rear lot.  Mr. Wing states 
the purpose was to perhaps build in the future, but in the meantime to have a larger backyard.  Mr. 
Wing also notes that at the time he was not aware of the legal doctrine of merger and that the lots 
would need to be subdivided.  He also notes that his family is growing and that they will soon 
outgrow their existing space, and that the intent would be to move into one of the two new 
townhomes.   
 
Chair Vyedin opens the floor to public comment. 
 
Abigail Clark of 3 Skerry Street Court introduces herself as an immediate abutter.  Ms. Clark 
expresses objection to the proposal, noting the proximity to the property line and density.  Ms. Clark 
expresses concerns related to drainage and snow removal as well. 
 
Gretchen Buckley of 3 Skerry Street Court introduces herself as an immediate abutter.  Ms. Buckley 
suggests the request seems excessive, noting the proposal is for two three-story townhouses in a 
dense neighborhood with a dead-end street.  She also expresses concerns about fire safety and asks 
that the Board deny the requested relief. 
 
A resident of 4 Skerry Street Court introduces herself and expresses concerns regarding the petition 
and extent of the variances being requested.  She speaks against the petition and asks if there is a 
valid hardship to consider.  Concerns about privacy and density are also expressed. 
 
Ian Clark of 3 Skerry Street Court introduces himself as a direct abutter.  Mr. Clark speaks against 
the petition and suggests it would be a detriment to direct abutters and the neighborhood overall.  
Mr. Clark raises concerns regarding density and safety, and notes that a smaller single-family home 
was previously denied for this property based on density concerns.  He echoes concerns raised by 
others regarding drainage as well. 
 
Chair Vyedin notes a number of written public comments as well, and reads one of the letters from 
the owners of 4 Skerry Street Court.  The letter discusses the history of the lot as being considered 
unbuildable at the time of sale.  The letter lists conditions under which they would be comfortable 
with the petitioner going forward with construction, namely changes to height, size, and location.
City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals 
July 15, 2026 Meeting Minutes 
  7 
Ms. Orfanos notes that there appears to be a third story, which would require additional relief if 
plans remain as is.  The Board continues to discuss the petition and concerns raised.  The petitioners 
acknowledge that they will need to continue and come back with revisions and to address concerns 
raised by commenters and Board members. 
 
Ms. Simpson is curious about how the trees might be able to remain, and also would like to see the 
back side of the proposed townhouses from Skerry Street Court.  She also reiterates concerns 
regarding drainage.  The petitioner notes that one tree will need to be removed, but that others will 
be trimmed and preserved.  Mr. Habib suggests a site plan showing abutting properties. 
Melinda Hager of 6 Skerry Street introduces herself and questions the petitioner’s need for a two-
family structure.  She suggests something more appropriately sized for the lot would be better and 
asks that the Board ask questions about alternatives.   
 
Pat Frederickson of 1 Skerry Street Court introduces herself and speaks against the petition, noting 
that the proposal is too large and infringes upon abutters’ privacy.  Ms. Frederickson also contends 
that the petitioner currently utilizes the first floor as a short-term rental, and claims the need for 
additional space is unfounded.  She echoes concerns raised by other commenters and asks that the 
Board come down to look at the neighborhood. 
 
Heather Roman of 8 Skerry Street introduces herself and raises concerns regarding the amount of 
relief being requested.  Ms. Roman acknowledges the need for housing and suggests an ADU might 
be more appropriate.  She expresses concerns regarding density and drainage. 
 
The Board continues to discuss the petition, comments, and updates to the variance requirements, 
and asks the petitioner if they would like to continue.  The petitioner agrees. 
 
Motion and Vote: Ms. McGaha motions to continue the petition of GRAHAM WING (formerly 
Graham Hines) at 7 BURNSIDE STREET and 5 SKERRY STREET COURT (Map 36, Lot 0157; 
Map 36, Lot 0149) (R2 Zoning District) for a Variance per Section 4.1.1 Dimensional Requirements 
of the Salem Zoning Ordinance to divide an existing merged parcel and construct a two-family 
house at 5 Skerry Street Court. The proposal would create a 4,393-square-foot lot at 7 Burnside 
Street with a 2,196-square-foot lot area per dwelling unit, and a 3,820-square-foot lot at 5 Skerry 
Street Court with a 1,910-square-foot lot area per dwelling unit, thirty-seven-foot frontage, and 
insufficient front, side, and rear setbacks. The petition will continue to the next regularly scheduled 
meeting of the Zoning Board of Appeals on August 19, 2026. 
 
Ms. Simpson seconds the motion.  The vote is five (5) in favor (Elena Eimert, Ellen Simpson, 
Christa McGaha, Peter Habib, and Nina Vyedin) and none (0) opposed.  The motion 
passes. 
 
   
Location: 23 Jackson Street (Map 25, Lot 0661) (R2 Zoning District) 
Applicant: Brian G. Sims and Robert G. Hahn
City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals 
July 15, 2026 Meeting Minutes 
  8 
Project: A public hearing for all persons interested in the petition of BRIAN L. SIMS and 
ROBERT G. HAHN at 23 JACKSON STREET (Map 25, Lot 0661) (R2 Zoning 
District) for a Variance per Section 4.1.1 Dimensional Requirements and a Special 
Permit per Section 3.3.5 Nonconforming Single- and Two-Family Residences of the 
Salem Zoning Ordinance to construct a sunroom, attached two-car garage, and a 
modified entry deck to a nonconforming single-family house, increasing the lot’s 
coverage from 25.4% to 36% where 35% is required. 
 
 
Documents and Exhibitions     
• Application date-stamped June 4, 2026, and supporting documentation 
 
Chair Vyedin introduces the petition. 
 
Attorney Bill Quinn introduces himself on behalf of the petitioner and describes the property and 
intention to keep the property as a single-family dwelling.  Mr. Quinn indicates that the petitioners’ 
needs have changed over time, and that they no longer utilize an above-ground pool located on the 
property.  This will be replaced with the garage, sunroom, and entry deck proposed, which would 
replace the pool.  Mr. Quinn presents a plot plan showing existing and proposed conditions, as well 
as a dimensional table.  He also describes the relief being requested.   
 
Chair Vyedin asks clarifying questions regarding the setbacks shown on the plot plan and whether 
the garage is attached or not, as that matters with respect to which variance(s) are required.  Chair 
Vyedin suggests looking at the proposal holistically and then examining the two variances required 
(for lot coverage and setback or distance from dwelling, depending on whether the garage is 
attached or not). 
 
Project architect David Harmon introduces himself and presents additional details regarding the 
proposal.  Mr. Harmon shares elevations and additional plans showing existing and proposed 
conditions.  Chair Vyedin asks about the curb cut, which Mr. Harmon indicates will likely be 10 to 
12 feet, certainly below the city limit.  
 
Chair Vyedin asks about the easement shown on the plans.  Mr. Quinn indicates it is with the 
property at 25 Jackson Street and was established many years ago when some of the land was 
divided.  The permanent legal easement has no effect on any of the setbacks.  The Board asks 
additional clarifying questions.   
 
Chair Vyedin opens the floor to public comment, but there is none.   
 
The Board continues to discuss the petition and relief, and Chair Vyedin suggests a special condition 
where the existing driveway be changed to a permeable material, but Ms. Eimert notes that is already 
in the project plans.  The Board discusses a special condition to update the dimensional table to 
correct the side setback.   
 
Motion and Vote: Mr. Habib motions to approve the petition of BRIAN L. SIMS and ROBERT 
G. HAHN at 23 JACKSON STREET (Map 25, Lot 0661) (R2 Zoning District) for a Variance per 
Section 4.1.1 Dimensional Requirements and a Special Permit per Section 3.3.5 Nonconforming

Single- and Two-Family Residences of the Salem Zoning Ordinance to construct a sunroom, 
attached two-car garage, and a modified entry deck to a nonconforming single-family house, 
increasing the lot’s coverage from 25.4% to 36% where 35% is required.  The approval is subject to 
the following standard conditions: 
1. Petitioner shall comply with all city and state statutes, ordinances, codes, and regulations. 
2. All construction shall be done as per the plans and dimensions submitted to and 
approved by the Building Commissioner. 
3. All requirements of the Salem Fire Department relative to smoke and fire safety shall be 
strictly adhered to. 
4. Petitioner shall obtain a building permit prior to beginning any construction. 
5. The exterior finishes of new construction shall be in harmony with the existing structure. 
6. A Certificate of Occupancy is to be obtained. 
7. A Certificate of Inspection is to be obtained 
8. Petitioner is to obtain approval from any City Board or Commission having jurisdiction 
including, but not limited to, the Planning Board. 
9. Unless this Decision expressly provides otherwise, any zoning relief granted does not 
empower or authorize the Petitioner to demolish or reconstruct the structure(s) located 
on the subject property to an extent of more than fifty percent (50%) of its floor area or 
more than fifty percent (50%) of its replacement cost at the time of destruction.  If the 
structure is demolished by any means to an extent of more than fifty percent (50%) of its 
replacement cost or more than fifty percent (50%) of its floor area at the time of 
destruction, it shall not be reconstructed except in conformity with the provisions of the 
Ordinance. 
10. All construction shall be done per the plans and dimension submitted to and approved 
by this Board.  Any modification to the plans and dimensions must be approved by the 
Board of Appeals unless such changes are deemed a minor field change by the Building 
Commissioner in consultation with the Chair of the Board of Appeals. 
11. Petitioner shall schedule Assessing Department inspections of the property, at least 
annually, to project completion and a final inspection upon project completion. 
 
And the following special condition: 
   1.  The petitioner shall submit a revised dimensional table for the stamped plot plan dated  
        May 11, 2026 by the oath Shore Survey Corporation, stating the primary structure’s  
        existing side setback, prior to receiving a building permit from the Inspectional Services  
        Department. 
 
Ms. Simpson seconds the motion.  The vote is five (5) in favor (Nina Vyedin, Elena Eimert, 
Christa McGaha, Ellen Simpson, and Peter Habib) and none (0) opposed.  The motion 
passes.

Project: A public hearing for all persons interested in the petition of ISRAEL BERL at 2 
ROCKDALE AVENUE (Map 09, Lot 0157) (R1 Zoning District) for Variances per 
Section 5.1.5 Parking Design and Section 5.1.6(2) Setbacks of the Salem Zoning 
Ordinance to create an additional curb cut for a five-car parking area. The proposal 
would create a forty-five-foot curb cut with a parking space approximately one foot 
from the side property line where two feet are required. 
 
 
Documents and Exhibitions     
• Application date-stamped June 8, 2026, and supporting documentation 
 
Chair Vyedin introduces the petition. 
 
Israel Berl introduces himself on behalf of the petitioner and describes the proposal to create an 
additional curb cut for a driveway that was previously increased in size.  Mr. Berl presents plans 
showing existing and proposed conditions, and notes the driveway expansion previously approved.  
He notes the owners are struggling with parking and have received several parking violations for 
parking on the street, and explains the need for additional spaces driving the proposal.  The 
requested curb cut is roughly 45 feet wide.  Mr. Berl also discusses drainage and other details. 
 
Chair Vyedin asks why the petitioner requires so much parking.  Mr. Berl explains the garage is not 
currently used as a garage and the current difficulties with parking in the existing concrete driveway.  
Mr. Berl also notes there are four individuals in the home with cars that require space to park. 
 
Chair Vyedin expresses safety concerns regarding the large curb cut.  Mr. Berl explains the location 
and specific proposal more, noting ledge in other parts of the property that limit the options of 
where additional parking can go, as well as required turning angles.  Ms. Orfanos offers that the 
parking violations referenced by the petitioner were due to parking business vehicles and operating a 
business in an R1 zone.  Ms. Orfanos also notes one of the proposed spaces backs into a crosswalk.  
Board members discuss concerns regarding the size of the request.  Mr. Habib suggests he would be 
more comfortable with two spaces rather than the proposal.  Mr. Larrick notes the proximity to a 
local school and the importance of sidewalks in the area.    
 
Chair Vyedin opens the floor to public comment, but there is none. 
 
Chair Vyedin discusses the options before the petitioner with respect to going to a vote, continuing, 
or withdrawing without prejudice.  Mr. Berl asks to continue the petition to the next regularly 
scheduled meeting.  Board members provide additional feedback. 
 
Motion and Vote: Ms. Eimert motions to continue the petition of ISRAEL BERL at 2 
ROCKDALE AVENUE (Map 09, Lot 0157) (R1 Zoning District) for Variances per Section 5.1.5 
Parking Design and Section 5.1.6(2) Setbacks of the Salem Zoning Ordinance to create an additional 
curb cut for a five-car parking area. The proposal would create a forty-five-foot curb cut with a 
parking space approximately one foot from the side property line where two feet are required. The 
petition will continue to the next regularly scheduled meeting of the Zoning Board of Appeals on 
August 19, 2026.
